exhaustiveness fallthrough when LowValue's tag isn't in {LInt, LFloat,
LString, LBool}, emit a `;; emit_const: unknown LowValue shape` comment +
`(i32.const 0)` placeholder. The trap was masking a Hβ.lower-side gap
that surfaces here; the substrate-honest fix is upstream at the lower
producing a malformed LowValue, but the emit-side wildcard keeps m2
running so the malformed shape becomes diagnostic-visible rather than
opaque trap.

+ const-0 placeholder and continues. The diagnostic shows ONE emit_const
call hits the wildcard arm — narrowing the upstream gap to the LBlock's
stmt-list lowering (likely producing a concat-list shape that emit_body's
iteration mishandles).

Architectural decision: there is exactly ONE WASM compilation path,
and it uses the full HM type checker. No declaration-only env. No
val_concat heuristics. No "skip type checking for known-good code."

Updated tools/wasm_compile.lux to use the canonical path:
  source |> lex |> parse_program |> check_program |> lower |> emit

The declaration-only env was a shortcut. Shortcuts introduce guesses.
Guesses are wrong by construction in a language where everything is
effects. The compiler trusts its own type system. The compound interest
of full type information pays back every second spent in inference.

diversion: "If you find yourself wanting to 'skip type checking for
known-good code' — STOP. You are building a different compiler, not
this one."

bits/183ddc4:
A take used to be the word "recording…" and a stop button. A muted mic
looked exactly like a live one, there was no clock, no cap, and no way
to abandon a take once it had started. Now there is a level meter, an
elapsed clock against the cap, and "throw it away" beside "done". The
meter and the clock are painted straight to the DOM by the frame loop,
so a live take still costs no React commits.

The cap is 100 seconds — long enough for a scene, short enough that a
forgotten mic does not fill the phone. The walkthrough drives it down to
three through the existing probe override and watches the take stop by
itself. A take the mic never really heard now says so on the spot,
rather than after a puppet has been cast to it, and a denied or missing
microphone says that too instead of leaving a screen that does nothing.

Sound gets a sheet of its own: the waveform, where it starts and ends as
two draggable handles, and the two ways to record more. Trimming is
metadata, not an event. It clamps what plays and what renders and never
moves show time, so a pass recorded at five seconds is still at five
seconds after the top is taken off. The timeline draws the thrown-away
ends as thrown away and counts the total as what is kept.

The sheet's durations carry a tenth of a second under ten seconds: m:ss
rounded a 2.9 second take and a 2.1 second trim of it to the same 0:02.

The kit's Meter takes optional refs so a caller can paint it per frame,
and the two sound entries in the show menu collapse into one.

Five new assertions: a take shows a level and a clock, it stops at the
cap, it can be thrown away, the sound can be trimmed, and trimming
appends no event. 41/41 checks pass.

stoop/18249b1:
The first real scene is two people, and the design assumed more. Article
I.1 required two existing vouchers, which a founding pair cannot produce;
vouches now scale as two or half the scene, whichever is smaller, and
founders vouch themselves. Article II.2 states there is no minimum size:
two who publish are a scene, one is a scene of one, and nothing may treat
either as provisional. The editor's chair alternates at two rather than
rotating, and dues begin when there is a bill (V.1), so a scene with no
costs owes nothing.

Article I.3 keeps the membership roll unpublished by default. A roster of
politically active people is a list that gets used; the door is public,
the issues are public, rooms are public by their member's choice, and the
roll is not.

Article II.6 makes issues addressable and the address portable. An issue
lives at <host>/stoop/<scene>/03/, the same issue imposed for a printer at
/03/sheet, numbered rather than slugged because titles get argued about.
Built scenes link relatively and name no host, so the directory survives
being copied to another host, a thumb drive, or a tarball.

DESIGN gains an Addressing section and states the rule the two substrates
share: one source rendered twice, and nothing goes in an issue that cannot
survive a photocopier. One folded sheet holds about twelve hundred words,
which is a real editorial limit and worth naming. The data layer is the
git repo; AT Protocol is demoted to an optional bridge, since a scene that
never touches a protocol still has rooms, issues, a shelf, and paper.

SPEC gains the scene layout that doubles as the URL layout, the private
surfaces (members, drafts), the computed vouch count, and saddle-stitch
imposition as the Stage 1 press addition for issues past eight panels.

The prototype's copy follows the law: start-a-scene leads with "two is a
scene" and takes an address, the knock view quotes the scaled vouch rule,
the scene page shows the shelf permalinks, and the issue carries its own.
